identityStatements.content: Do the small thing today, not the perfect thing someday.
Money I don't spend is time I get back.
Rest is part of the plan, not a reward for finishing it.
If it isn't written down, it isn't real.
Progress over streaks. Miss once, never twice.

journalEntries.content: Paid the card down another $180. It is finally under $3,200.
Skipped the takeout twice this week. Cooking is not the hard part — deciding is.
Rough day at work. Did not log anything. Starting again today.
The automatic transfer is the single best thing I set up.
Sunday review took four minutes. I keep expecting it to hurt.
Almost bought the espresso machine. Parked it instead.
Walked home instead of the rideshare. Small, but it counts.
Groceries came in under budget for once.
Tired. In bed by 10:30 and it fixed most of it.
Called about the interest rate — no luck, but I asked.
First month where savings went up and the card went down.
Missed two habits today. Not going to miss them tomorrow.
Told a friend about the payoff plan out loud. Felt real.
Bought the book instead of the gadget. Fine trade.
The uncategorized transaction was a vet bill. Mystery solved.

notes.title: Debt payoff plan
notes.content:
The whole plan on one page.

1. Minimums on everything.
2. Every spare dollar at the [[Visa card]].
3. Keep [[Emergency fund]] at one month while paying down, then build to three.

Reviewed every Sunday — see [[Sunday money review]].

#money #goal

notes.title: Visa card
notes.content:
Balance was $6,810 in the spring. Now it is under $3,200.

Rate is 22.9%. Asked for a reduction, was declined once — ask again after six on-time payments.

Every extra dollar here beats every dollar in savings until it is gone. See [[Debt payoff plan]].

#money #debt

notes.title: Emergency fund
notes.content:
Target: three months of costs, about $8,400.

At $3,420 today. Holding at one month until the [[Visa card]] is clear, then the whole payment redirects here.

#money #safety

notes.title: Sunday money review
notes.content:
Four minutes, same order every week:

- File anything uncategorized
- Check the surplus against target
- Move whatever is left at the card
- Write one line in the journal

Shorter than I expect it to be, every time. #ritual #money

notes.title: Groceries that actually get eaten
notes.content:
Buying less, more often, beats one big shop I half-use.

Rotation: beans, eggs, rice, whatever green is cheap, one thing I actually want.

Cuts [[Eating out]] more than any rule I have tried. #food #money

notes.title: Eating out
notes.content:
Not the enemy — the unplanned ones are.

Rule: planned meals out are intentional and get marked that way. Everything else is a leak.

#food #money

notes.title: Sleep is the lever
notes.content:
Every week I sleep badly, the spending goes up and the goal hours go down. It shows in the numbers, not just my mood.

Bed by 11. See [[Evening shutdown]]. #health

notes.title: Evening shutdown
notes.content:
Dishes, phone on the charger across the room, ten pages, lights out.

Twenty minutes. Protects [[Sleep is the lever]] better than any alarm. #ritual #health

notes.title: Things I stopped buying
notes.content:
Second streaming service. Delivery fees. The gadget I wanted in March and cannot now name.

Total: about $74 a month, doing nothing but leaving.

#money

notes.title: Why this goal
notes.content:
Not about the card. About never again having a $600 surprise decide my next three months.

When it gets boring, this is the note to reread. #goal #motivation
